newsitem.title: USA: Scattered showers likely for U.S. Midwest, Plains.
newsitem.headline: Scattered showers likely for U.S. Midwest, Plains.

text.p: Scattered showers were forecast early this week for the U.S. Midwest and High Plains, however the driest wheat areas in northern Kansas may not receive significant rain until the weekend, forecasters said.

"The area that needs it most are the northwest and northcentral (Kansas) districts," said Joel Burgio, Weather Services Corp meteorologist, who said he expected scattered amounts of 0.10 to 0.30 inch there Tuesday.
A second storm system forecast for the Plains this weekend offers a greater chance for rain, but forecasters believe the system's greater rain amounts will miss the dry wheat areas.

"It looks like northern Kansas and Colorado really need a lot of rain, but we don't hold a lot of hope for that area to get rain for the next 10 days," said Craig Solberg, Freese-Notis Weather meteorologist.
Solberg said so far, April rainfall in northwest Kansas is 25 percent of normal.
"I'm not optimistic for meaningful rain there," he said.

WSC's Burgio said the weekend system has the potential to produce 0.25 to 1.00 inch of rain in the Plains, but the greatest amounts may fall across eastern areas of Nebraska, Kansas, Oklahoma and Texas.
In the Midwest, rain amounts of 0.30 to 1.50 inches were likely Tuesday in Iowa and Missouri and then Wednesday across Illinois, Indiana, southern Michigan and southern Wisconsin, said Burgio.
A second system Friday and Saturday in the Midwest should produce 0.50 to 1.50 inches along the same path, with lesser amounts along the Ohio River Valley.
"We would most likely see planting delays because of rain," said Burgio of this week's precipitation. "Next week looks like it may open up a little bit," he said of prospects for clearer weather.
Solberg said Monday and early Tuesday in the Midwest should be dry with rain expected late Tuesday, which should benefit planted corn.
"I think there is a good number of farmers who would like a good shower right now," he said.
Farmers, recalling previous years of rain-delayed plantings, actively sowed corn last week despite cool soil temperatures.
Solberg said warmer-than-normal weather was likely for the western Midwest this week and cooler than normal in the east, but neither area should have extreme cold or heat.
